builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Muting Tokens: Exploring Token Sparsification for Efficient Audio Transformers
summary: It replaces full-token transformer processing for audio spectrogram patches with token pruning or merging guided by attention scores and spectral cues. The cost is an added token-scoring/selection stage, possible fine-tuning, and implementation complexity in the inference path, with compute savings dependent on how many tokens can be removed safely. It can fail when quiet, low-frequency, or short transient events carry task-critical information, when domain shift invalidates the chosen spectral cue, or when pruning ratios are tuned on one dataset or model size and transferred to another.
rationale: This is relevant to single-GPU audio inference because it reduces transformer token load without training a foundation model, but the provided evidence is comparative rather than quantified and explicitly varies by dataset, duration, and model size, so the reader should run a workload-specific A/B test before production adoption.
technique: Frequency-aware token sparsification for audio transformers

claims.statement: It replaces full-token transformer processing for audio spectrogram patches with token pruning or merging guided by attention scores and spectral cues. The cost is an added token-scoring/selection stage, possible fine-tuning, and implementation complexity in the inference path, with compute savings dependent on how many tokens can be removed safely. It can fail when quiet, low-frequency, or short transient events carry task-critical information, when domain shift invalidates the chosen spectral cue, or when pruning ratios are tuned on one dataset or model size and transferred to another.

The paper reports that frequency-aware sparsification, especially spectral flatness and low-frequency energy cues, consistently outperforms attention-only pruning, while spectrogram patch intensity is especially effective for longer audio inputs; no numeric speedup or accuracy delta is given in the abstract.
